eda01_sentences_by_split_source.caption: SkillSpan: sentences per split (train 4,800 / dev 3,174 / test 3,569), coloured by source (tech vs house).

eda01_tokens_per_sentence.caption: Tokens per sentence by source; 99% of sentences are shorter than the 128-token training limit.

eda01_span_length_hist.caption: Span length distribution (tokens): skill spans are multi-word verb phrases (median 4), knowledge spans are mostly 1–2 tokens.

eda01_top_skill_phrases.caption: The 30 most frequent skill phrases in the training split — dominated by soft skills ('communication skills', 'team player').

eda01_top_knowledge_phrases.caption: The 30 most frequent knowledge phrases in the training split — programming languages, frameworks and degrees.

eda01_pos_patterns.caption: Part-of-speech patterns of spans: skills are VERB+… phrases or NOUN+NOUN ('communication skills'); knowledge is PROPN/NOUN heads.

eda01_ngrams_tech_vs_house.caption: Top bigrams per source: tech postings are about software development, experience and flexible working; house postings mix application boilerplate ('further information', 'please contact') with business domains ('supply chain', 'project management').

eda01_entities.caption: spaCy entity labels in SkillSpan sentences: ORG/GPE are mostly scrubbed to placeholders; DATE and CARDINAL ('3+ years') dominate what remains.

eda01_tagged_example.caption: A SkillSpan sentence with its merged BIO tags (blue = skill, orange = knowledge).

eda02_label_status_by_subset.caption: Label status per benchmark subset: in TECH ads about 43% of annotated skill phrases cannot be mapped to ESCO (mostly LABEL NOT PRESENT) and 37% in HOUSE — the gap the 'not in ESCO' detector targets; TECHWOLF has sentence-level ESCO labels only.

eda02_top_esco_labels.caption: The most frequent ESCO target skills: a long tail — the top 25 skills cover only a small share of phrases, so retrieval must handle thousands of rare labels.

eda02_esco_label_length.caption: Token length of the ~13.9k ESCO skill labels: most are 2–5-word verb phrases ('manage musical staff'), which is why a bi-encoder (not keyword match) is needed.

eda02_sentence_length.caption: Sentence length per subset: TECH sentences are shortest (median ~10 tokens), HOUSE sentences the longest (median 15–18 tokens).

eda02_spans_per_sentence.caption: Number of annotated skill phrases per sentence: most sentences carry 1–3 phrases; a few list-style sentences carry 10+.

eda02_unmapped_terms.caption: Phrases annotators could not map to ESCO 1.1.0: concrete frameworks, tools and platforms (ReactJS, Docker, Django, Spring, Azure, Node.js…) — exactly the vocabulary a job-matching product must track outside the taxonomy.

p1_f1_comparison_test.caption: Problem 1: strict and loose span F1 per approach and span type on the SkillSpan test split (identical sentence set for all approaches; tagger = mean over seeds).

p1_false_positives_test.caption: Problem 1: over-extraction on sentences without any gold span (headers, benefits) — how often each approach invents a span where annotators found none.

p1_f1_by_source_test.caption: Problem 1: strict span F1 split by posting source (tech vs house) — the domain gap each approach suffers.

p2_workrb_map_val.caption: Problem 2: WorkRB MAP per task on the val split for lexical and dense baselines, the fine-tuned bi-encoder (champion) and retrieve-then-LLM (challenger).

p2_workrb_rp10_val.caption: Problem 2: WorkRB RP@10 per task on the val split for lexical and dense baselines, the fine-tuned bi-encoder (champion) and retrieve-then-LLM (challenger).

p2_workrb_mrr_val.caption: Problem 2: WorkRB MRR per task on the val split for lexical and dense baselines, the fine-tuned bi-encoder (champion) and retrieve-then-LLM (challenger).
